questions.question: A documentation test needs only the documentation build, but it waits for an unrelated eight-minute API build in the same stage. Which change addresses that barrier directly?
options: Declare the documentation build with needs
Add a cache with a global key
Retry the documentation test
Store the source as an artifact
questions.explanation: An explicit needs edge lets the test start when its real producer finishes instead of waiting for every job in the earlier stage.

questions.question: What happens when every dependency is complete but all eligible runner slots are busy?
options: The job remains queued
GitLab ignores runner tags
The job reuses another job's process
The pipeline skips the job
questions.explanation: Dependencies make a job ready; an eligible runner still has to claim it. Capacity queueing is separate from graph ordering.

questions.question: Which file transfer should remain correct even when the runner cache is empty?
options: A build artifact consumed by deployment
A package-manager download cache
A reusable compiler cache
A branch-local dependency cache
questions.explanation: The promoted build output is a correctness input and belongs in an artifact contract. A cache is optional acceleration and must be rebuildable.

questions.question: Why use workflow rules in addition to job rules?
options: To decide whether a pipeline should be created for a source
To increase runner concurrency
To encrypt artifacts
To make a shell runner ephemeral
questions.explanation: Workflow rules are evaluated for pipeline creation. Job rules decide which jobs appear in a pipeline that exists.

questions.question: Which runner is the best match for code from an untrusted fork?
options: An ephemeral unprivileged build runner without production credentials
A persistent shell runner holding deployment keys
A privileged shared runner on the GitLab host
A protected production runner with an untagged job
questions.explanation: Untrusted repository code needs a disposable, constrained execution boundary and no production authority. Tags and protection rules complement but do not replace isolation.

questions.question: What problem does resource_group solve for two production jobs targeting the same environment?
options: It serializes jobs that share the named deployment resource
It verifies the artifact digest
It creates an OIDC trust policy
It makes both deployments interruptible
questions.explanation: A resource group limits concurrency for the named resource so overlapping pipelines do not mutate the same target simultaneously.
